R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.finding: The prior loop-dynamics lowering fixture was not admitted end-to-end by the current grammar: the fixture used a named cycle header not accepted by current/minimal-repair grammar, and its Python lowering treated emit as terminating return although no such explicit G9 emit-terminator semantics was established.
R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.materiality: In a 20000-case discriminator, return-lowering versus nonterminating-emit behavior differed in 17693 cases. Therefore prior loop-dynamics results remain useful as manually constructed behavior/mechanism fixtures, but they do not establish ClayCode source-to-target semantic preservation.
R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.evidence_downgrade: Any fused statement treating those loop-dynamics proxy runs as compiler-chain evidence is superseded. Only their controlled dynamics/mechanism observations survive at the narrower fixture evidence class.
R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.new_gate_rule: BASE evidence requires an unbroken, content-addressed source -> production parse -> canonical typed IR -> checked lowering -> executable target -> replay receipt chain. Manual/generated target equivalence is insufficient when the source is not admitted or lowering adds semantics.
R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.counterhypothesis: The observed source/fixture differences could be limited to research fixture syntax and not affect the eventual frozen production grammar/lowering after frontend closure.
R4_SOURCE_PARSE_IR_LOWERING_CHAIN_BREAK.falsifier: After frontend closure, the same representative programs pass production parse/type/effect/lowering and differential execution with no unexplained semantic divergence.

R5_SECOND_GENERATION_HYPOTHESES.reason: New transformed ClayResearch hypotheses are hypothesis generation, not independent evidence. They remain candidates for later discrimination and do not modify scientific claim status in this refresh.
